data.description:
## testing_mode: RED

## What
Add tests to tests/scripts/ (or tests/) that verify _handle_edit.py does not overwrite local bug-type-* tags when Jira sends different labels. Tests fail because the preservation logic doesn't exist yet.

## Check first
Find the existing test for _handle_edit.py: grep -rl '_handle_edit' tests/
Read those tests to understand the test fixture pattern.

## Tests to write
Using the existing test pattern for _handle_edit.py:

1. Scenario: local ticket has tags ['bug-type-scope-drift', 'review:complete'], Jira sends labels ['review:complete'] (drops the bug-type tag). Assert the resulting edit_fields['tags'] still includes 'bug-type-scope-drift'.

2. Scenario: local ticket has tags ['bug-type-scope-drift'], Jira sends labels ['new-jira-label']. Assert resulting tags include BOTH 'bug-type-scope-drift' AND 'new-jira-label'.

3. Scenario: local ticket has tags ['review:complete'] (no bug-type tags), Jira sends labels ['different-label']. Assert the result overwrites normally (no bug-type tags to preserve).

4. Scenario: local ticket has tags ['bug-type-scope-drift'], Jira sends labels [] (empty). Assert no tag edit is triggered (existing empty-Jira-labels safeguard still works).

## File to create or modify
Either add to an existing test file for _handle_edit.py, or create tests/scripts/test-handle-edit-tag-preservation.sh or tests/test_handle_edit_tag_preservation.py.

## Done when
Tests fail RED (preservation logic doesn't exist yet in _handle_edit.py).
data.title: [RED] Write failing test: _handle_edit.py preserves bug-type-* tags during Jira inbound sync
